title: Only mark orders refunded on full refunds in the mock service
objective: Make issueRefund (and its effect-log replay path applyResolvedOperation) set an order's status to "refunded" only when the refund amount covers the full order total, so a partial refund leaves the order at its pre-refund status exactly as the sealed goal annotations assert.
statement: Applying this change raises task_success_rate on the tau-style e2e task set by at least 0.2 (task-004-partial-refund flips from failed 2/3 to passed 3/3, so the set goes 4/5 to 5/5) and flips the current check-goal-orders failure member from failed to passed, without regressing any golden case; it is falsified if task-004 still fails goal:orders or task-001/002/003/005 regress. Evidence: grading the current code's partial-refund execution through projectServiceState reproduces the recorded failure exactly (projected digest 9fb5299f65db1088be30ac5652e9837d9826aa345d3c9ee242094249b12c3202 equals actual_sha256 of run-e2e-task-004-partial-refund-after-a9f986ed), while the full-refund-only status rule grades task-004 3/3 and keeps task-001 (full refund) and task-003 (refusal) at 3/3.

regressions.summary: No existing unit test (tests/workflow-tools.test.ts) or dal evaluation fixture asserts partial-refund order status — all exercise full refunds (amount == total), which remain "refunded" under the new rule — so test_pass_rate is not expected to move; a focused partial-refund unit case should be added in the same change.

The checked-in compiled plugin artifact lib/service.js is rebuilt from src in this tree and the dsh runtime loads lib/, so it must be regenerated in the same change to avoid loaded behavior diverging from src; the change alters no API or schema signatures.
